prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Miami. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I can pull up 4–6 specific, reputable implant practices in Miami (with phone numbers and a short reason to call each). To make the list most useful, please tell me:

- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Miami (e.g., Downtown, Coral Gables, Miami Beach), and  
- Any preferences: price/insurance, need for sedation, same‑day teeth/All‑on‑4, or a preference for academic/teaching clinics.

While I wait for that, here are immediate, practical recommendations and how I'll choose which offices to call for you:

Which kinds of providers to call (and why)
- Board‑certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — they do complex extractions, bone grafting, and implant placement under sedation; good for difficult cases.  
- Board‑certified periodontists — specialists in the gums and bone; many focus on implant placement and aesthetics.  
- Prosthodontists — specialists in designing and restoring implant crowns, bridges, and dentures; call them if you need the replacement tooth (the crown) carefully matched and planned.  
- Implant centers/ multidisciplinary practices — convenient if placement and restoration are coordinated in one office.

Good, quick places to search or filter providers (I can do this for you)
- American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) “Find a Surgeon”  
- American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) directory  
- ADA “Find a Dentist” (filter for periodontist/prosthodontist)  
- University of Miami School of Dentistry clinic — good academic option for quality care at often-lower cost

Key questions to ask when you call (so you can compare)
- Is the implant placed by a board‑certified oral surgeon/periodontist or a general dentist?  
- Do you do CBCT 3D imaging in-office? (important for safe planning)  
- Which implant brand(s) do you use and why? (well-known brands are Straumann, Nobel/Biotecnica, Zimmer, etc.)  
- Will the same office handle the crown/restoration, or will I be referred to another dentist?  
- Do you offer sedation or IV anesthesia?  
- Do you do bone grafts or sinus lifts if needed? How often?  
- Expected timeline and total estimated cost (implant + abutment + crown, and any bone grafting)  
- Options for same‑day/teeth‑in‑a‑day / All‑on‑4 if I’m interested  
- Financing or payment plans, and whether you accept my insurance

Red flags to avoid
- No in‑office CBCT or no ability to take a 3D scan when needed.  
- No clear estimate or unwillingness to explain what’s included.  
- Pressuring you to accept immediate pricey options without a full evaluation.  
- Very low prices with no explanation of the implant system or the clinician’s experience.

If you give me your Miami neighborhood/ZIP and priorities, I’ll produce a short list of specific offices to call with phone numbers and the reason to call each.
